newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle exit 1996 on lower note.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle exit 1996 on lower note.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures ended the final session of 1996 lower, with a mix of technical and cash-connected selling occurring throughout the session, traders said.

Most of the selling appeared to be profittaking and light hedging after strong gains Monday. Sources said Monday's gains may have appeared excessive and were anxious to take profits. End-of-the-month and year-end selling also may have been a factor, they said. Cash markets failed to offer much support.
A small number of feedlot cattle traded at $67.00 per cwt Tuesday, a price traders had expected.
CME livestock markets closed at 1200CST/1800GMT Tuesday and will be closed Wednesday in observance of the New Year's holiday.
Commercial selling weighed on feeder cattle prompted by the decline in live cattle, traders said.
Live cattle closed down 0.900 to 0.300 cent with February off the most at 64.975. Feeder cattle were off 0.675 to 0.300 cent with January off 0.675 at 67.525.
